content_voiceover: This flowchart, from the Taiwan Society of Hematology multiple myeloma guideline, outlines the initial treatment pathway for newly diagnosed disease. After diagnosis, every patient is assessed for disease burden, performance status, organ function, comorbidities, cytogenetics by FISH, and staging, and clinical trial enrollment should always be considered if available. The central decision point is transplant eligibility. Transplant eligible patients receive a triplet or quadruplet combining a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory drug for three to six induction cycles, followed by high dose melphalan conditioning and autologous stem cell transplant, then optional consolidation and maintenance therapy. In select cases, if a patient is concerned about high dose chemotherapy toxicity and induction has already achieved a deep response, transplant can be deferred. Transplant ineligible patients instead receive a doublet, triplet, or quadruplet PI and or IMiD based regimen continued as ongoing therapy. Both pathways converge at relapse, which triggers subsequent line therapy.
keypoints: Transplant eligibility is the key branch point after initial disease assessment
Transplant-eligible: PI/IMiD triplet or quadruplet induction for 3-6 cycles, then autologous stem cell transplant
Post-transplant: optional consolidation followed by maintenance therapy
Transplant-ineligible: continuous PI and/or IMiD-based doublet, triplet, or quadruplet therapy
Transplant can be deferred if induction achieves a deep response and the patient wants to avoid high-dose chemo toxicity
keypoint_voiceover: The core decision for newly diagnosed myeloma is transplant eligibility. Eligible patients get induction with a PI plus IMiD, high dose melphalan, autologous transplant, then maintenance, with consolidation as an option in between. Ineligible patients get continuous combination therapy without transplant. Both pathways eventually meet at relapse, prompting subsequent line therapy, and transplant can occasionally be deferred if induction already achieves a deep response.
